citeinfo.title: CSD.csv: Spatial variability in environmental DNA concentrations on river cross sections: implications for sampling design and abundance estimation

pubinfo.publish: Dryad (data release); code and data also at GitHub

descript.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) concentrations of the myxozoan parasite Ceratonova shasta (organismal eDNA, actinospores) and of Chinook salmon Oncorhynchus tshawytscha (extra-organismal eDNA) were measured by droplet digital PCR in 192 one-liter water samples collected on six cross sections of the Klamath River, California, 16 to 22 April 2021. On each cross section 15 to 19 verticals were sampled at the surface (grab) and at 60 percent of depth (US DH-59 isokinetic sampler), with water velocity, depth, and discharge measured at each vertical. The data support an analysis of within-cross-section variability of eDNA concentration, spatial generalized linear mixed models, and sample size calculations for estimating the mean eDNA concentration of a river cross section. This file is the analysis dataset read by the main script (R_code/Main_Analysis_and_Figures.R).
descript.purpose: To quantify spatial variability of eDNA concentration across river cross sections and to inform the number and placement of water samples needed to estimate the mean eDNA concentration of a cross section to a chosen precision.
descript.supplinf: Companion to Keel, D. J., N. A. Som, M. J. Henderson, and A. P. Kinziger (in prep.), Spatial variability in environmental DNA concentrations on river cross sections: implications for sampling design and abundance estimation. Column definitions follow the usage in the analysis script. Site codes as used in the field; the manuscript numbers the sites 1 to 6 from upstream to downstream. Bounding coordinates are approximate.

attracc.attraccr: ddPCR reactions with fewer than 10,000 accepted droplets or without clear separation of positive and negative droplets were rerun (less than 10 percent of reactions). A random subset of extracts (25 for C. shasta, 23 for O. tshawytscha) was run twice to assess measurement error. Limits of detection were 6.3 (C. shasta) and 11.8 (O. tshawytscha) copies per reaction; samples below the limit of detection are recorded as zero in the analysis. No-template controls and field blanks were below the limit of detection.

dataqual.logic: Each row is one water sample or one reaction. Sample identifiers link the field sheet, the ddPCR output, and the analysis dataset.
dataqual.complete: All 192 surface and depth water samples from the six cross sections are present in CSD.csv. The field sheet also lists depth-integrated samples and field blanks that were not used in the published analysis.

procstep.procdesc: Water samples (target 1 L) were collected 16 to 22 April 2021 at 15 to 19 verticals on each of six cross sections of the Klamath River, one at the surface (Whirl-Pak bag) and one at 60 percent of depth (US DH-59 isokinetic sampler). Velocity (Price AA meter at 20 and 60 percent of depth), depth (sounding reel), and distance from the bank (tape on a static line) were recorded at each vertical; discharge was computed by the midsection method.

Samples were filtered in the field within 10 hours (47 mm, 5 um cellulose nitrate). DNA was extracted by acetone dissolution of the filter followed by the Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue protocol with a 100 uL final elution. Each 22 uL ddPCR reaction (Bio-Rad QX200) contained 15 uL of extract and species-specific primers and probes for C. shasta (HEX) and O. tshawytscha (FAM); Poisson-corrected copies per reaction were estimated by Bio-Rad QX Manager 1.2.
Copies per liter of water were computed as copies per reaction x elution volume (uL) / 15 uL x volume filtered (mL) / 1000, in R_code/Main_Analysis_and_Figures.R of the repository.

enttyp.enttypd: Analysis dataset: one row per one-liter water sample (192 rows), with its position on the cross section, hydraulics, volume filtered, elution volume, and ddPCR results for C. shasta and O. tshawytscha.
